selection_rationale: CNSM26-03 best balances novelty, falsifiability, computational feasibility, and reproducibility for a five-page CNSM short paper. The critic review marked it as “pass” with high reproducibility and feasibility scores, and its proposed grounding metrics map directly to operational correctness (RAG/tool confirmation → sandbox pass) supported by prior work on tool-augmented agents and grounding (e.g. W4404782868, preprint 202604.1820.v1). This candidate enables a compact, machine-verifiable experiment with clear primary outcomes suitable for the track and fewer unresolved ethical/dual-use concerns than the adversarial-poisoning and high-fidelity-sandbox benchmark proposals.
unresolved_uncertainties: Metric generalization: to what extent do grounding metrics (source-coverage, provenance-diversity, tool-confirmation-score, conflict-score) generalize across different retrieval backends and LLM families?
Normalization: how to normalize provenance signals and token-level source support across heterogeneous retrieval systems and tokenizers to allow comparable metric computation?
Tool-confirmation circularity: do tool-confirmation signals introduce circular evidence when tools and retrieval share underlying data, biasing correlation with sandbox-correctness?
Holdout/selection leakage: how to ensure holdout/threshold-selection procedures avoid leakage and produce calibrated early-warning thresholds in practice?
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Provide precise, implementation-level definitions and reference implementations for each grounding metric including edge cases and tokenization choices (public code and examples).
Specify normalization procedures to make provenance and token-support signals comparable across heterogeneous retrieval backends and document the normalization math and defaults.

Include at least one additional pipeline/model variant (or explicitly bound conclusions to the evaluated pipeline) to test metric generalization; document model identifiers, prompt templates, and seeds.

Pre-register holdout split generation, nested cross-validation and threshold-selection procedures (including random seeds and stratification rules) to prevent leakage and ensure valid holdout performance estimates.
